app.title: Celestia · Orbital Lab
app.summary: The person picks two bodies from a catalogue, or enters custom masses or places them by clicking the map, and sets their separation. The interface derives the mass ratio and solves for the five equilibrium points. The person chooses one point, which gets a stable or unstable verdict, and then nudges a test particle's starting position and velocity away from it. Each change runs a forecast over three orbital periods. The person views it as a 2D map, a 3D potential surface or an animated playback, reads off summary quantities, and can export the run as a video.

task.text: Disturb a test particle at an equilibrium point of a two-body system and simulate whether it stays near the point or escapes.

data.text: No data is loaded. A model system is set by two masses and a separation, and each forecast produces a sampled trajectory over time. An effective-potential surface is computed over the plane.
data.item: a simulated trajectory of a test particle started near one equilibrium point

stage.text: exploring how a model system responds to disturbances, by simulation

mechanism.text: Sidebar forms set the system, the equilibrium point and the perturbation, and every change reruns the forecast. A central plot draws the result in one of three modes, with playback controls, and clicks on it can place custom bodies. A row of summary numbers and an export dialog sit around it.

field.text: restricted three-body simulation in celestial mechanics

workflow.name: perturb a model from an equilibrium and simulate its response

steps.here: Choose primary and secondary bodies from a catalogue, or enter custom masses, and set the separation with a slider. The mass ratio is derived and shown, the masses are swapped if the secondary is heavier, and a reset button returns to the default pair.

steps.step: choose a starting point and check its stability
steps.here: A radio picks one of five equilibrium points, and nothing is forecast until one is picked. A linear-stability check by eigenvalues labels the point a stable region or an unstable saddle.
Sliders move the start point in/out and sideways and trim its velocity. A reset button zeroes all three.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each change integrates the test particle for three orbital periods with an adaptive integrator, stopping early if it escapes, and rotates the result into the co-rotating frame.

steps.step: look at the result in alternative views
steps.here: Switch the plot between a cinematic inertial playback, a 2D rotating-frame map and a 3D effective-potential terrain. Play and pause, change the speed, or scrub a timeline. On the map, two clicks place custom bodies and set their separation.
A telemetry row reports the maximum deviation from the start point, the Jacobi constant, the mass ratio and the orbital period.
Once a forecast exists, an Export video button renders the trajectory as an MP4 in a dialog, with a download button.

distinctive: The result is shown in the frame that co-rotates with the two bodies, where the equilibrium points stay fixed.
Each equilibrium gets a stability verdict computed from eigenvalues, so the person knows beforehand whether to expect libration or escape.
A conserved quantity (the Jacobi constant) is reported next to the deviation, as a check on each run.
Custom bodies can be placed by clicking two points on the map, and their separation is taken from the clicks.
